behaviour-switch.answer: The switch is DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Control/DialectBehavior.cs:301), read only by CompileTimeArithmetic.For (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeArithmetic.cs:44), which picks the mode for operand entry and + - * / inside a compile-time arithmetic expression (§2002:7.2.5.2 GR1; its 34-digit 2002 mode against §2002:8.8.1.3.1.1's 32 digits is the known PB5575-family defect, reaching only results of arithmetic operations). A single numeric literal operand of DEFINE is a literal, not an arithmetic expression (§2002:7.2.9.3 GR5), so literal-1 never enters the arithmetic mode the switch selects. Re-run now at --std 2002: eval_basic.cob prints DEF-NUM-OK, DEF-ALNUM-OK, DEF-BOOL-OK, DEF-NAT-OK and DEF-FRAC-OK (1.5 kept, where an arithmetic expression would be truncated to its integer part by §2002:7.2.5.2 GR2) (E:\COBOL-coord\scratch\op-20261114\read-2002\out-answer\probes-a-03\run-evalbasic-2002.log).
